the addition of hydrolysates in WPI-based cast films significantly changes the film properties, which is caused by a reduction in the average molecular weight of the protein.

the use of hydrolysed proteins in whey protein based cast films leads to a reduction of the molecular weight of the protein, which leads to a reduction in the mechanical properties, while the permeability remains unchanged.
the addition of hydrolysates in WPI-based films can be used to reduce the brittleness of WPI-films without affecting the barrier performance.

the influence of hydrolysates in whey protein-based films.

hydrolysed WPH has an impact on the film properties and can be considered as a promising additive to improve the film flexibility and thus the processability.
the addition of hydrolysate WPI in whey protein-based films can be an effective tool in order to reduce the brittleness of the films while maintaining their barrier properties.

the addition of hydrolysates in whey protein films leads to the formation of more flexible films with lower mechanical properties.

hydrolysed wheys can be used as a substitute for native wheys, but with some restrictions, especially in the food industry.
